The Local

Concept 4 · Direction: Local expert

This concept answers ‘why buy here rather than online?’ with people and place. The first thing you see is the team outside the Ringwood centre and a real photo from the shop floor, and the headline names the town. The fitters get faces, roles and the brands they fit; the centre gets opening hours, a sketch map and directions. The Motocaddy range sits in arch-topped frames that feel tactile rather than catalogue-like, and membership is presented as joining a club with a physical card, with the £60.90 saving told as a plain-English sum. The palette comes from the New Forest heath (heather, bracken, gorse) rather than golf-course green, and the body face is chosen for legibility, which matters to the older golfers who buy most trolleys.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

‘The people you’ll meet’ and ‘The centre’ are added straight after the hero, ahead of the trolley range: in this concept the people are the reason to buy, so they come first. The three pillar tiles and the trust row are dropped; trolleys, fitting and membership each get a full section instead. Reviews and buying guides share one section. A ‘Come and see us’ section with a sketch map is added near the end.

Typefaces

HeadlinesYoung Serif (400)Google Fonts, SIL OFL. A soft, slightly chunky serif: friendly rather than elegant, so it avoids the default ‘elegant serif’ look.
Body and UIAtkinson Hyperlegible (400/700)Google Fonts, SIL OFL. Designed by the Braille Institute for low-vision readers; very clear at small sizes, which matters to the older golfers who buy most trolleys.

Key components (rendered from the concept’s own CSS)

Buttons. Rounded (10px), bracken with white text; gorse on dark bands. A secondary action is an underlined link with an arrow, not a second button.

Book a free fittingShop Motocaddy trolleys

Product card. An arch-topped frame on Mist with the cut-out, the full model name (set in Atkinson bold, because Young Serif’s old-style figures make “M5” read like “M₅”), one friendly spec line, price and stock in words.

Imagery and photography

Real people, real place: the team, the centre, customers mid-fitting, trolleys on New Forest heathland and local courses. Natural light, slightly warm grade, candid rather than posed. Arch-topped frames for portraits and products give a consistent, tactile shape.

The hero already uses one real shop photo (approved used Srixon irons on the hitting mat); more of these work better than stock imagery.

Headline copy

H1: “Ringwood’s home for Motocaddy trolleys and fitted clubs.”

Sub: “Book a free, no‑obligation fitting with our team, or shop the 2026 Motocaddy range. Members get back more than they pay in.”

Section heads: “The people you’ll meet” · “A fitting with us” · “Join the club” · “Come and see us”

Motion

Gentle: photos fade in as you scroll, and the membership card tilts slightly on hover. Nothing that competes with the photography.

Trade-offs

Does wellStrongest on trust, the fitting service and membership-as-belonging; the most clearly ‘not a national chain’; Atkinson Hyperlegible makes it the most readable for older trolley buyers; the sketch map and hours make visiting easy.
Weaker onLives or dies on photography of real people; without it the page is a lot of placeholders. The trolley range sits lower than in the other concepts, and the page is longer, so online-only buyers far from Ringwood may find it less relevant. Needs staff willing to be featured.
Build effortLow–medium: simple components; the map is an illustration; arch frames are pure CSS.
Photography neededHigh: team portraits, the centre, fittings in progress and trolleys on local courses. A half-day shoot would cover it.
Suits bestGolfers within driving distance of Ringwood, first-time trolley buyers who want advice, members, and older golfers who value service over price.

EG monogram: ‘EG’ in Young Serif, gorse on a heather rounded square; also used as the membership card mark (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
